author: Codex first-pass author C

source_artifacts.claim: Current roster places Cargo Exchange at campaign position 16 after level_10 and before level_12.
The authored scene gives each hero a delivery pad that latches the barrier on the partner route.
Current level geometry, two counterweight decks, four latch pads, barriers, empty authored hazard set, crates, optional receipts, and exits.
Heroes and ordinary crates each weigh one; loads include supported bodies, and deck movement is enabled only when each deck has a hero, with direction determined by the load difference.
Moving decks carry supported riders/cargo, constrain movement against geometry, and move in opposite vertical directions.
Any-hero pads count ordinary crates and heroes toward minimum weight; a latch stays active after its weight leaves.
Hazard collision and falling below the world can kill; the mandatory route and authored geometry must therefore be assessed separately from the empty hazard list.

evidence.claim: Earlier subtitle says a hero’s latch opens the partner’s lane and powers the stair.

prior_knowledge.concept: Two counterweight decks move only with one hero on each, and their supported load difference determines direction; cargo placement changes that balance.

mechanics.fact: The left and right decks travel through a 270-unit exchange. A hero must ride each deck for movement; the supported load difference, including ordinary crates, chooses which deck descends.

evidence.claim: The paired decks have 270 units of travel and speed 65.
Hero/crate weights form each load; both rider flags gate the direction, which follows the load difference.
At frame 12 Isp is on cargo_right while Pac is on left_upper_dock; the initial one-rider state is not yet a two-deck ride.
At frame 72 Pac and outbound_ballast are on cargo_left while Isp remains on cargo_right, consistent with the route beginning after Pac boards and gets the sac aboard.

mechanics.fact: The lower-dock arrival pad latches an inner recovery gate. The cargo_parked pad needs weight two; Pac plus the ordinary outbound sac supply the two units and latch the return-cargo gate.

evidence.claim: The lower arrival pad latches the inner gate; cargo_parked is an any-actor pad with minimum weight two and latches return_cargo_gate.
An accepted hero contributes one; an ordinary crate contributes one; latches persist after the actors leave.
At frame 576 Pac has reached the lower deck and lower_dock_arrival is latched, opening the inner recovery gate.
At frame 792 Pac and outbound_ballast share cargo_parked; the pad has weight 2, latches, and opens return_cargo_gate.

mechanics.fact: Isp activates DELIVERY at the right upper dock to latch Pac’s upper-left route open, then boards the return sac on the right deck; Pac later activates RETURN to latch Isp’s lower-right route open.

evidence.claim: Isp’s DELIVERY opens pac_delivery_gate and Pac’s RETURN opens isp_delivery_gate.
The authored scene associates those pads with reciprocal partner barriers.
At frame 900 Isp is on the right upper dock; isp_delivery is latched and Pac’s barrier is open.
At frame 1122 the return ballast is aboard cargo_right while Isp is on the right upper dock preparing the return ride.
At frame 1848 Pac’s RETURN pad is latched and Isp’s barrier is open.

steps.action: Isp rides the right deck; Pac crosses from the left upper dock onto the left deck.
steps.expected_feedback: With a hero supported on each deck the clutch permits movement; the deck direction follows the load difference, not rider presence alone.
steps.observed_feedback: In the native replay Pac moves right onto cargo_left while Isp remains on cargo_right; outbound_ballast is also supported on cargo_left at the sampled frame.

evidence.claim: The panel explains the both-rider clutch and displays each deck’s rider/load state.
The deck movement condition and direction depend on both riders and relative load.
Native trace shows Pac and the outbound sac on cargo_left and Isp on cargo_right at frame 72.

steps.goal: Ride the left deck down and reach the lower dock.
steps.action: Remain aboard while the heavier left deck descends; step onto the lower-left dock after arrival.
steps.expected_feedback: The lower_dock_arrival latch opens the inner recovery recess when Pac reaches it.
steps.observed_feedback: At the sampled frame 576 Pac is on cargo_left at the lower level and lower_dock_arrival is latched; the inner recovery gate is open.

evidence.claim: The lower dock and latched lower-arrival gate provide the landing and recovery recess.
Native trace state at frame 576 has Pac on the lower deck and the lower-arrival latch open.

steps.goal: Release the return cargo and keep access to the left deck.
steps.action: Move onto the lower-left recovery area and push the outbound sac onto CARGO PARKED so Pac and the sac jointly meet the pad’s weight requirement; then return to cargo_left.
steps.expected_feedback: The two-weight latch opens return_cargo_gate and stays open after Pac leaves.
steps.observed_feedback: At frame 792 Pac and outbound_ballast occupy cargo_parked, weight is 2, and return_cargo_gate is open; at frame 828 Pac has reboarded cargo_left and the latch remains set.

evidence.claim: The pad requires weight 2 and latches the cargo gate.
A hero and ordinary crate each contribute one unit and a latch persists.
At frame 792 the hero-plus-sac state yields pad weight two and opens the gate.
At frame 828 Pac is back on cargo_left and the cargo latch remains open.

steps.goal: Open Pac’s exit route and obtain the return sac.
steps.action: With Pac still on cargo_left, Isp crosses to the upper-right DELIVERY pad, then pushes return_ballast from the right dock onto cargo_right.
steps.expected_feedback: Isp’s latch opens pac_delivery_gate; placing the sac aboard increases the right-side load for the return exchange.
steps.observed_feedback: At frame 900 Isp is on right_upper_dock with isp_delivery latched and Pac’s gate open; by frame 1122 return_ballast is supported by cargo_right.

evidence.claim: The Isp delivery pad latches the barrier on Pac’s route.
A supported crate contributes to the right deck load and changes the load difference.
At frame 900 the DELIVERY latch is set and Pac’s gate is open.
At frame 1122 the return sac is supported by cargo_right.

steps.goal: Return Pac to the upper-left dock and Isp to the lower-right dock.
steps.action: Reboard the left and right decks with Pac and Isp respectively. The right deck carries Isp plus return ballast and descends as the left deck rises; leave each deck at its matching dock.
steps.expected_feedback: The opposing decks exchange levels while carrying their riders and cargo; the latched cargo/delivery routes remain open.
steps.observed_feedback: At frame 1632 Pac is back at left_upper_dock and Isp is on cargo_right at lower level; at frame 1752 Pac is at left_upper_dock and proceeds to RETURN.

evidence.claim: Relative deck loads determine opposite travel once both riders are present.
The two platforms move in opposite vertical directions and carry supported bodies.
At frame 1632 the native trace has Pac at the left upper dock and Isp on the lower part of cargo_right.
At frame 1752 Pac is on the left upper dock while Isp remains aboard the right deck.

steps.goal: Latch both reciprocal exits and finish.
steps.action: Pac activates RETURN on the upper-left pad and reaches the left exit; Isp leaves the right deck for the lower-right exit after Pac’s latch opens his barrier.
steps.expected_feedback: Pac’s arrival opens Isp’s exit barrier; both matching exits complete the room.
steps.observed_feedback: At frame 1848 Pac’s return latch is active and Isp’s barrier is open; at frame 1917 both heroes are at their exits, with zero deaths.

evidence.claim: The partner-specific delivery pads open the matching exits and define both exit locations.
At frame 1848 Pac’s RETURN latch is active and the Isp barrier is open.
The ordinary-input native route completes both exits at frame 1917 with zero deaths; this establishes feasibility, not human difficulty or control reliability.
Current native ordinary-input route completes level_23 at frame 1917 with both exits and zero deaths; it is expert feasibility evidence only.

isp: Occupies cargo_right for the two-rider clutch.
Activates Isp-only DELIVERY to latch Pac’s route open.
Moves the return sac onto cargo_right so the second load balance sends the decks back.
Rides the right deck down and reaches the lower-right exit after Pac latches RETURN.
pac: Boards cargo_left and pushes the outbound sac aboard to create the initial load difference.
Rides down, reaches the lower-left dock, and shares the two-weight CARGO PARKED pad with the outbound sac.
Reboards the left deck for the return exchange, then activates Pac-only RETURN and exits at upper left.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assume the decks move with only one hero aboard, or step off a deck before the partner reaches the other.
common_mistakes.consequence: The rider interlock sets movement direction to zero while a hero is missing from either deck; the intended exchange pauses.
common_mistakes.recovery: Return to the nearby dock or remain in the bounded shaft, put one hero on each deck, and restore the needed cargo balance. This recovery is inferred from the implementation and continuous walls, not observed in a human attempt.

evidence.claim: Without a rider on each deck the direction is zero.
The authored geometry comment states that full-width decks and continuous walls keep missed boarding inside the shaft.
Upper/lower docks, recovery stops, walls, and broad decks bound the exchange area.

common_mistakes.mistake: Stand alone on CARGO PARKED and expect it to latch, or leave the outbound sac off the marked pad.
common_mistakes.consequence: One ordinary hero contributes only weight one, below the visible two-weight requirement, so the return-cargo gate stays shut.
common_mistakes.recovery: Move the outbound sac onto the pad and stand with it; once latched, the gate remains open after leaving. The exact retry was not tested with novice input.

evidence.claim: The visible panel shows CARGO PAD: 0/2 WEIGHT.
The cargo pad requires two units and latches its gate.
An ordinary hero and ordinary sac each contribute one; latches persist.

common_mistakes.mistake: Board both decks but leave the return sac on the upper-right dock, expecting the second exchange to reverse direction.
common_mistakes.consequence: With no cargo changing the loads, the deck movement may stop or travel the wrong way for the desired return; the rider clutch alone does not select direction.
common_mistakes.recovery: Push the return sac onto cargo_right, keep one hero on each deck, and let the new load difference take effect. This source-inferred recovery was not tried as a human mistake.

evidence.claim: An ordinary crate contributes one unit of supported load.
Direction is the sign of the load difference, gated by one rider per deck.
The replay places return_ballast on cargo_right before the second deck exchange.

optional_collectibles: outbound_receipt (Pac) is placed at the lower-left dock; it is not required for either exit.
return_receipt (Isp) is placed at the upper-right dock; it is not required for either exit.

reasoning.rationale: Several linked causal decisions remain: put both riders on separate decks, make the intended deck heavier with a sac, use Pac plus the outbound sac to meet the lower cargo pad threshold, then rebalance the opposite deck and trigger reciprocal arrival latches. The panel exposes rider/load state but does not state how the load difference chooses direction.

evidence.claim: The panel exposes the two-rider clutch and load state but not the direction rule.
Movement depends on both rider presence and relative weight.
Lower cargo and reciprocal delivery pads create an ordered set of latch dependencies.

cooperation.rationale: Both heroes are functionally required on different decks for movement, then take distinct pad/cargo roles. Pac enables the first delivery and return latch; Isp enables the reciprocal delivery and provides the return load. The dependency repeats across the exchange, although the route does not require simultaneous button presses.

evidence.claim: A rider must be present on both separate decks for movement.
Cargo and hero-specific latches create reciprocal contributions.
The native route uses both heroes in sequence to latch both routes and complete both exits; this does not measure human coordination.

execution.rationale: The mandatory route requires controlled boarding, pushing two sacs onto decks/pads, stepping between deck and dock, and reboarding for the return. The broad decks, full-width platforms, and bounded walls reduce precision demand; the native route does not require a chain of narrow jumps.

evidence.claim: Full-width decks, continuous walls, docks, and recovery stops bound missed boardings.
The route boards Pac and the outbound sac onto the left deck.
The route boards the return sac onto the right deck before the return exchange.

timing.rationale: The mandatory movement has no timed window: deck direction responds to current riders and supported loads, and delivery/cargo pads latch. The trace can pause at milestones; no deadline or cycle has to be caught.

evidence.claim: The decks respond to rider/load state rather than a time window.
Latched pads stay active after their triggering weight leaves.
The route can leave the cargo pad after it latches; later state retains the open gate.

hazards.rationale: No required step crosses an active hazard: this room authors no hazard geometry, and the mandatory route stays on the decks, docks, and bounded recovery areas. That judgment uses the route geometry as well as the empty hazard set; the general fall-death rule remains relevant only if a player leaves those safe regions.

evidence.claim: Broad docks/decks and continuous walls define the mandatory transfers and keep missed boardings in the shaft.
The mandatory pads/barriers and exits are reachable along the bounded docks; the authored hazards list is empty.
The current route completes both exits without a death; this is feasibility evidence, not a human failure-rate estimate.

novelty.rationale: Earlier rooms expose shared lifts, nutrient-sac cargo, heavy cargo, and partner-opening latches. This room recombines those familiar themes around a new counterweight model: both decks need riders, supported load controls direction, and two cargo deliveries reverse the exchange. Prior exposure supports transfer but does not establish mastery.

evidence.claim: Earlier level introduces a lift requiring two cells.
Earlier level introduces a nutrient sac as plate duty.
Earlier text introduces heavy marrow cargo and a heavier DNA wall.
Earlier text introduces a latch that opens a partner lane.
The novel mechanic is the rider-gated, load-directed pair of decks.

recovery_cost.rationale: The likely first mistakes are reversible: without both riders the decks stop, an underweight cargo pad simply stays unlatched, and bounded docks/recovery stops provide a way to reposition and retry. The cargo and route setup can require extra travel, but no mandatory hazard reset is designed into the sequence. No human recovery attempt was observed, so this is a source-based estimate.

evidence.claim: Missing a rider stops movement rather than imposing a timed failure.
The source-authored bounded shaft, broad decks, docks, and recovery stops support repositioning after a miss.
A pad can be retried until it activates; once latched it persists.

solution_clarity.rationale: The central panel explicitly gives the two-rider rule and live load state, and the dialogue names one nutrient sac each and partner-arrival doors. Players still need to discover the central load-direction relation and infer how the lower two-weight cargo latch sequences the reciprocal deliveries, leaving a noticeable but not wholly hidden causal link.

evidence.claim: Visible instructions identify the clutch, both deck states, and a two-weight cargo pad.
Dialogue names the nutrient sacs and says DNA doors open on someone else’s arrival.
The screen’s load state has a causal movement effect not explained in the visible text.

control_friction.rationale: No two-human simultaneous-input/reliability trial is available. A scripted native route demonstrates that the sequence is feasible but cannot establish shared-keyboard conflicts or input-response reliability.

evidence.claim: Native scripted route establishes feasibility only; it is not a two-human control test.

confidence_reason: Current source establishes the rider gate, relative-load direction, cargo thresholds, latches, bounded route geometry, and exits. The current native replay verifies one ordinary-input both-exit route with no deaths. No novice pair, control-reliability trial, or actual mistake/recovery attempt was observed; recovery and the ratings are expert estimates rather than player outcomes.

confirmed: Pass one correctly identified that the panel requires one rider on each deck, shows load state, and sets a two-weight cargo threshold. The source confirms the rider clutch and the ordinary hero/crate weights; the trace shows Pac plus the outbound sac reaching weight 2 at cargo_parked.

Pass one correctly treated the delivery/return sequence, hazard consequences, recovery, and control friction as unresolved from idle frames. Source and trace now resolve mechanics and route feasibility, but not novice discovery, human recovery, or two-person reliability.
missed_mechanics: The rider clutch alone does not determine travel: the decks move only with a hero on each, while the sign of left-load minus right-load selects direction. Pac must get the outbound sac onto the left deck for the first exchange; Isp later gets the return sac onto the right deck for the reverse exchange. Source counterweights.ts lines 70-110 and trace snapshots 2 and 11 support this.

The lower CARGO PARKED pad is a latched any-actor two-weight gate. Pac and the ordinary outbound sac supply one unit each; the trace shows weight 2 and the return gate open at snapshot 6. Isp DELIVERY and Pac RETURN are separate hero-specific latches that open the partner’s route, as shown in level_counterweight.ts lines 75-107 and snapshots 8 and 16.

The geometry provides broad decks, continuous walls, docks, and recovery stops; missing a boarding or arriving underweight does not inherently impose a lethal hazard or timer. This supports low source-inferred recovery burden, not a measured retry rate.
incorrect_inferences: Pass one listed the green area and figure as possible mandatory hazards, but the current room’s authored hazard list is empty and its scene defines dialogue/partner-gate schemes rather than a harmful route obstacle. The native route stays on bounded decks and docks. The general fall-death rule remains, so this conclusion rests on route geometry, not an assumption that all falls are safe.

Pass one marked the two-deck clutch/load model as entirely new. It is still a new counterweight mechanic, but earlier rooms already cue two-cell lifts (level_01), shared-lift/split-route play (level_45), nutrient-sack plate use (level_08), heavy cargo (level_09), and partner latches (level_11); the newness is in their load-directed exchange and sequencing rather than those component ideas alone.
changed_judgments: Reasoning stays 3: the panel makes the rider and cargo thresholds visible, but it does not state that load difference controls direction or show the reciprocal order. Source lines 101-110 plus route snapshots 2, 6, 11, and 16 establish the interacting dependencies.

Cooperation stays 3, now supported by distinct necessary contributions: one hero per deck, Pac’s lower cargo pad and RETURN latch, and Isp’s DELIVERY latch and return-sack placement. This is sequential mutual dependence rather than a simultaneous-input window.

Execution changes 3 to 2 because the source and successful route show pushes, dock-to-deck transfers, and reboarding, but full-width decks and bounded approaches reduce precision; the native mandatory route does not require sustained narrow jumps.

Timing changes from unknown to 0 because direction is state/load-driven and pads latch. The native route pauses between deliveries without a timed window; this is supported by the movement and latch implementations, not inferred from its completion duration.

Hazards changes from unknown to 0 because the actual required path stays on decks/docks in bounded shafts and no authored hazard intersects it. Empty hazards alone would not prove safety; source geometry, fall behavior, and the route trace were considered together.

Novelty remains 3 but is reframed: the counterweight clutch and load-direction relation are new, while shared-lift, cargo, and partner-latch ideas have earlier visible introductions. This recombination still creates a new model to learn.

Recovery changes from unknown to 1 because an underweight pad can be retried, a missing rider merely stops motion, and source comments/geometry provide bounded recovery spaces. This remains a mechanic-based estimate; no human error/retry was tested.

Solution clarity stays 2: visible text explains the clutch and threshold and dialogue signals reciprocal delivery, but neither explains that cargo balance selects direction or lays out the exchange order. Control friction remains null because scripted feasibility is not two-human reliability evidence.
unresolved: Whether a first-time pair notices that both decks need heroes before testing the cargo, and whether the live load display is enough to infer which deck will descend.
Whether the weight-two panel and one-sac-each dialogue lead players to use Pac plus a sac on CARGO PARKED without extensive trial and error.
Actual novice mistake rates, recovery time after misplaced cargo, and shared-keyboard control friction are not measured by the native replay.

single_operator_note: The baseline assumes two humans. A single operator would need to switch between both heroes while arranging the paired deck loads and pushing cargo, but that additional task switching is not scored in the two-human ratings.
